decision: Apply the protected rectory main-building point as the canonical 1814 anchor and retain the yard and reconstructed Wilse garden as secondary site context.
identityFindings: The intended entity is the protected Spydeberg rectory main building, not Spydeberg settlement or a generic rectory locality.
Norwegian heritage ID 86078 covers a protected rectory complex including the main building, storehouse, yard and garden.
The main building is the event anchor because Christian Frederik held the council meeting there on 8 August 1814.
The reconstructed Wilse garden and the wider protected site remain important secondary historical layers.
eventFindings: Christian Frederik held a council meeting at the rectory on 8 August 1814 while the war with Sweden was under way.
The decisions and subsequent developments led toward the negotiations and the Convention of Moss on 14 August.
The Constitution was adopted at Eidsvoll and the Convention was concluded in Moss; neither event should be relocated to Spydeberg.
Spydeberg's precise role is the council, headquarters and decision-making stage in the crisis between Eidsvoll and Moss.

siteContext.gardenContext: Jacob Nicolai Wilse's eighteenth-century formal garden has been reconstructed from drawings, written descriptions and garden-archaeological investigations.
